title: State ag boards seeking member nominations - NewsBreak
text:
By Staff Reports ,
6 hours ago Positions are open on several state boards dealing with agriculture. The Tennessee Department of Agriculture is currently accepting nominations for the Wine and Grape Board, Forestry Commission, Equine Health Advisory Commission and Soil and Water Conservation Commission.
Wine and Grape
The Tennessee Wine and Grape Board is a seven-member board established to support the growth of Tennessee’s wine industry. The Board reports annually to the governor and to the General Assembly regarding the wine industry and viticulture in Tennessee. Positions on the Board are appointed by the governor and allocated under state law to members from specific sectors of the industry.
Members serve a four year term and are not eligible for compensation or per diem expenses arising from their service.
The Tennessee Department of Agriculture is currently accepting nominations for three positions on the Board: One member who is a grape or fruit producer in the state, one member who has a background in higher education and fermentation or viticulture and one member who is involved in production, marketing, sales, journalism or education regarding the Tennessee wine industry
To submit a nominee for consideration, please provide the following by Jan. 5: nominee’s full name and contact information, the specific position for which they are being nominated and a brief description of the nominee’s qualifications, including relevant professional and public service experience
Submit nominations to: tn.agriculture@tn.gov or Tennessee Department of Agriculture, Business Development Division, Attn: Kacey Troup, PO Box 40627, Nashville, TN 37204.
Soil and Water
The Tennessee Soil and Water Conservation Commission is an 11-member body established to administer and approve watershed districts, support the work of local conservation districts across the state, and maintain a statewide plan for conservation of Tennessee soil. Members serve a three year term and are not eligible for compensation but are eligible for travel reimbursement arising from their service.
The Tennessee Department of Agriculture is currently accepting nominations for one farmer or agricultural representative from the Eastern Grand Division.
To submit a nominee for consideration, please provide the following by Jan. 5: nominee’s full name and contact information, a brief description of the nominee’s qualifications, including relevant professional and public service experience.
Submit nominations to: tn.agriculture@tn.gov or Tennessee Department of Agriculture, Land & Water Stewardship Section, Attn: Dr. Sam Marshall, PO Box 40627, Nashville, TN 37204
Equine Health
The Tennessee Equine Health Advisory Commission is a nine member body established to study and make regulatory recommendations addressing equine health and industry issues in the state.
Members serve four year terms and are not eligible for compensation or reimbursement for travel or other expenses related to their service.
The Tennessee Department of Agriculture is currently accepting nominations for one member position.
Nominees must be legal residents of Tennessee and possess personal or professional experience and knowledge of the state’s equine industry.
To submit a nominee for consideration, please provide the following: nominee’s full name and contact information and a brief description of the nominee’s qualifications, including relevant professional and public service experience.
Submit nominations by Jan. 5 to: tn.agriculture@tn.gov or Tennessee Department of Agriculture, State Veterinarian Office, Attn: Jennifer Chambers, PO Box 40627, Nashville, TN 37204.
Forestry
The Tennessee Forestry Commission is a seven member body established to promote the protection and welfare of state forest resources; encourage multiple use and development of those resources; and create and monitor long-range planning to implement full use and conservation principles on state forest resources. Members serve a five year term and are not eligible for compensation but do receive travel reimbursement for expenses arising from their service.
The Tennessee Department of Agriculture is currently accepting nominations for two member positions: an owner of 500 acres or less of forests within the state; and a representative of a pulp and paper industry operating in the state.
To submit a nominee for consideration, please provide the following by Jan. 5: nominee’s full name and contact information, the specific position for which they are being nominated (forest landowner or industry representative) and a brief description of the nominee’s qualifications, including relevant professional and public service experience.
Submit nominations to: tn.agriculture@tn.gov or Tennessee Department of Agriculture, Forestry Division, Attn: Dyshea Brown, PO Box 40627, Nashville, TN 37204.
